first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Two of our strongest prior results show that signup simplification (memory_31) and shortening onboarding (memory_86) both produced durable lifts in activation and completion. These are directly addressing the current metric declines. Verifying these two memories ensures the prior methodology was sound before replicating at scale. While promotional_pricing addresses competitive pressure, it risks margin and doesn't address the core activation decline. Referral incentives work best for retention of established customers (not current problem). Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a lighter-touch complement but secondary to fixing the onboarding funnel itself. Enterprise_sales_assist doesn't address SMB activation. A standard_experiment on simplified onboarding targets sustainable qualified revenue by improving conversion efficiency rather than discounting, and builds on proven methods.

mid.rationale: Verification confirms both prior experiments. Memory_31 showed signup simplification drove +15% signups and +9% activation on SMB with +4% qualified revenue and only -1% retention impact. Memory_86 showed shortened onboarding achieved +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention lift. Current situation shows 6% activation decline and 4% onboarding completion decline QoQ—directly aligned with these proven levers. Simplified onboarding addresses root cause (funnel efficiency) rather than discounting into competitive pricing war or pursuing referrals (which work for retention, not activation). A standard_experiment applying simplified onboarding can be executed this week with high confidence of moving both activation and completion metrics while preserving long-term qualified revenue. No material downstream risk to retention given exp_86's +3% retention result.

final2.rationale: Situation has changed materially. Churn conversations with price-sensitive SMB have doubled this week due to competitive pricing attack. While simplify_onboarding remains sound for activation lift, it does not address immediate churn risk or competitive bleeding. Memory_73 confirmed targeted promotional pricing is effective for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. A small_guarded_test on promotional pricing can be deployed quickly to retain at-risk price-sensitive accounts and signal competitive responsiveness, buying time before simplified onboarding compounds long-term activation gains. This preserves the option to layer onboarding improvements later. Risk flagged: promotional pricing carries margin pressure and potential for unsustainable customer economics if overextended; small_guarded_test limits exposure while preserving ability to learn whether pricing pressure is temporary or structural. Uncertainty preserved on whether this addresses root churn drivers or merely delays decision.
